figures.label: Figure 17
figures.content: Entire continuous-time Markov-chain trajectory with three discrete states, including the complete Figure 17 caption
reading_notes: Time is continuous, while the state takes values in a discrete set.
Horizontal segments show a state being retained between random jump times; filled and open circles distinguish the state at a jump from its preceding value.
The example has sequence length d = 1 and three possible states.

figures.label: Figure 18
figures.content: Both general and factorized rate-matrix diagrams, with the complete Figure 18 caption
reading_notes: The grid illustrates a state space of sequences with d = 2 positions; each axis corresponds to one position.
An individual jump of a factorized CTMC changes only one sequence position, so arrows are axis-aligned.
Parallel-token Euler sampling can nevertheless change several positions within one finite step, with higher-order simultaneous-update probability.

figures.label: Algorithm 7
figures.content: Complete sampling algorithm: title, Require line, all twelve numbered steps, per-position Euler probability formula, and enclosing rules
reading_notes: The factorized rates are evaluated from the full current sequence before the per-position parallel updates.
For a finite step h, each position either stays or jumps according to a categorical Euler approximation.
The step size must make all categorical probabilities nonnegative; the displayed formula is not an unconditional guarantee for arbitrary h.

figures.label: Figure 19
figures.content: All ten panels of the conditional and marginal discrete probability paths, with the complete Figure 19 caption
reading_notes: Each grid cell is a discrete sequence state with d = 2; color indicates its probability mass.
The top row fixes one terminal data state, marked by an orange cross; the bottom row averages over data states.
These panels depict distributions, rather than successive states of one sampled trajectory.
In this chapter the generation-time direction runs from the initial distribution at t = 0 to the data distribution at t = 1.

figures.label: Algorithm 8
figures.content: Complete discrete-diffusion training algorithm: title, all Require lines, all fourteen numbered steps, corruption sampling, posterior prediction, loss, and parameter update
reading_notes: A Bernoulli value m_j = 1 retains the clean token z_j; m_j = 0 draws that position from the initial-noise marginal.
The network sees the whole noisy sequence and time, and predicts a vocabulary distribution for each position.
The training target is the original terminal token z_j; the displayed objective sums token-wise negative log-likelihoods.

figures.label: Figure 20
figures.content: All four rows of the masked language-model trajectory, including time labels, seven token positions, and the complete Figure 20 caption
reading_notes: The trajectory proceeds from all [MASK] tokens at t = 0 to a full sentence at t = 1.
Several different positions can be revealed in parallel, rather than strictly from left to right.
The diagram is an illustrative trajectory, not a claim that general CTMC sampling can never revise an existing token.
